title: Add a finite native icon and visual-token vocabulary for ConduitOS
body:
## Goal

Give the graphical ConduitOS Presenter enough reusable visual vocabulary to produce a coherent, polished UI without recreating CSS or a generic widget/theme framework.

This issue owns graphical Presenter styling mechanics beneath #3162 after text metrics are established.

## Required behavior

- Define a small bounded token table for spacing, inset, gap, border thickness, corner radius, foreground/background/accent/muted/success/warning/danger roles, and focus/hover/selection treatment.
- Define a pinned finite icon set for current shell concepts such as Body, Wake, Plan, Play, Host, Gear, Port, Line, run, close/back, confirm, warning/refusal, inspect, and status.
- Icons and tokens are graphical Presenter resources/mechanisms. Portable Presentation may express semantic role/importance/action meaning but does not name pixel sizes, colors, or icon asset IDs as semantic identity.
- Provide bounded lowering from semantic presenter roles to exact native graphics commands.
- Keep icon storage/raster work fixed and deterministic; no dynamic icon discovery.
- Ensure default controls and panels can be rendered consistently without each surface hard-coding its own arbitrary dimensions and paint choices.
- Preserve browser/native semantic convergence without requiring pixel parity.

## Required proofs

1. Workspace, inspector, status, and transient surfaces all use the same token vocabulary.
2. Current canonical shell actions display recognizable consistent icons where appropriate.
3. Hover/focus/selection/warning/success states are visually distinct and accessible without relying on color alone.
4. All icon and token storage is finite and admitted in the graphical profile.
5. Headless profiles remain unaffected.
6. Canonical live-ISO captures demonstrate one coherent default graphical language across all current shell surfaces.

## Stop line

No CSS selectors/cascade, arbitrary style inheritance, general theme marketplace, SVG/browser engine, dynamic icon packs, widget toolkit, animation framework, or GPU dependency.

## Dependency

Blocked by #3163 and contributes to parent #3162.
